item.title: US nationwide flight ground stop: "Our routers got overloaded with data"
item.description: On Friday, the Federal Aviation Administration issued a rare nationwide ground stop. More than 8,200 flights, or over 31% of those scheduled in the United States, were canceled. The ground stop lasted nearly five hours and was the longest in the country since September 11, 2001. Officials blamed outdated air traffic communications equipment, and said that there was no evidence of a cyber attack. The airspace is now reopened and flights have resumed. item.title: How Chinese custom ‘chong xi,’ or ‘clashing with joy,’ can counteract misfortune
item.description: In ancient China, when a man became seriously ill, his family might arrange a wedding for him in an attempt to drive away the disease. The custom is called chong xi, literally translated as “clashing with joy”. Its rationale is that a happy event could lift one’s spirits and thereby dispel illness or other misfortunes. In practice, if a man who was already engaged became seriously ill, his family might move his wedding forward. If he did not yet have a fiancée, his family might hastily find him...
